stories.headline: Houthi forces seize Yemen's Red Sea port of Mocha and advance toward the Bab al-Mandab Strait

sources.body: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels seized control of the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha on Thursday and were advancing towards the Bab al-Mandab strait, the Yemeni government and military sources said. The vital waterway serves as a key shipping lane linking Europe to Asia. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
sources.headline: Middle East live: Yemen’s Houthi rebels seize Red Sea port city Mocha

sources.body:
Forces loyal to the UN-recognised government and Houthis fight on multiple fronts in an effort to expand their control.

Sanaa, Yemen – The United Nations-recognised Yemeni government and the Houthi group have been using warplanes, missiles, drones and other weapons as they engage in intense fighting on multiple fronts in the country’s north, west and central regions.

At least 194 people have been killed and 880 others wounded in the past two weeks of fighting in parts of Taiz, the western coast, al-Jawf, Marib and Dhalea, according to aid agencies.

Iran-backed Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah (supporters of God), have intensified attacks on the coastal district of al-Makha (Mocha) located on the western coast, among others, to gain a foothold in the Red Sea – a vital shipping lane.

On the other hand, government forces have been battling to expand in Taiz and boost their control of Marib, an oil-producing region in the north.

Fighting has also been raging in the al-Jawf governorate bordering Saudi Arabia and Dhalea, which connects the Houthi-controlled north to the country’s south under the internationally recognised government.

Experts say gains or losses on any of these strategically important fronts could have significant consequences for either side.

“The hills and mountainous areas of Taiz and the western coast are key targets for the Houthis, who have repeatedly attempted to advance there,” Yazeed al-Jeddawy, the research manager at the Sanaa Center for Strategic Studies, said.

“The Houthis are trying to seize commanding terrains, cut supply routes between the coastal Mocha district and Taiz, and prevent government troops on the western coast from linking up with the Taiz Military Axis,” said al-Jeddawy.

In Taiz and along the western coast, al-Jeddawy says, the immediate contest is over the heights and roads connecting Taiz to al-Makha.

Situated roughly 60km (37 miles) from the Bab al-Mandeb strait, al-Makha enjoys a highly strategic position on the Red Sea. For a month now, the Houthis have launched missile and drone attacks on the city, causing massive damage to its port facilities and killing and injuring several civilians.

Recently, the group has also attempted to extend its ground operations towards al-Makha city.

“The Houthis seem intent on tightening their hold around [al-Makha] and moving closer to the Dhubab–Bab al-Mandeb area. A substantial advance would strengthen their position near the southern entrance to the Red Sea and give them greater leverage over international shipping,” he added.

Fuad Mussed, a Yemeni political analyst and author, told Al Jazeera that the strategic importance of the western coast and Taiz fronts stems from their proximity to Bab al-Mandeb, a chokepoint connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and one of the world’s most important shipping routes.

“The Houthis seek to move closer to this vital waterway to threaten maritime traffic. Such a move aims to keep the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb under the influence of Iran and use them as leverage against regional and international powers. This is a strategy Tehran has been pursuing for years,” Mussed said.
sources.headline: Houthis, Yemeni forces engaged in fierce battles: Why each front matters

stories.headline: UN nuclear watchdog says North Korea has built a new uranium facility

sources.body:
The International Atomic Energy Agency voices ‘serious concerns’ over expansion of Yongbyon facility to enrich uranium

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has voiced “serious concern” over evidence that North Korea has built a facility capable of enriching weapons-grade uranium to bolster its nuclear arsenal.

The new building, located at the the country’s main Yongbyon nuclear facility, can house up to 28 centrifuge cascades – machinery commonly used to enrich uranium – according to a report by the nuclear watchdog released this week.

The regime has also expanded operations at an enrichment site in Kangson, near the capital Pyongyang, according to the report, which was based on analysis of satellite imagery and open-source material, including photographs published by the country’s state media.

The IAEA, whose inspectors were expelled from North Korea in 2009 , identified the Yongbyon building as the site’s second uranium ‌enrichment facility after comparing satellite images taken during its construction with media photographs of a visit in early June by the country’s leader, Kim Jong-un .

During his visit, Kim claimed the North’s capacity to produce weapons-grade nuclear material had more than doubled over the past five years , according to state media, promising “vast future plans to exponentially strengthen the country’s nuclear forces”.

Citing a 2025 analysis by the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies in the US, South Korea’s Chosun Daily said the potential 28 cascades comprising 4,592 centrifuges at the Yongbyon facility could yield about 85 kg of weapons-grade highly enriched uranium a year – enough to build three or four additional warheads.

In a statement released this week, the IAEA’s director general, Rafael Grossi, said: “The ongoing operation of enrichment facilities at Kangson and Yongbyon and the reported further expansion of [North Korea’s] production of weapons-grade nuclear material is a cause for serious concern.”

“The continuation and further development” of North Korea’s nuclear programme are “clear violations of relevant UN security council resolutions and are deeply regrettable”, he added.

South Korea ’s defence minister, Ahn Gyu-back, said in August that the North possessed between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads – a much higher number than the 57 cited by Donald Trump the same month. The South Korean figure was based on estimates by private research organisations, Ahn told lawmakers, adding that the country’s military could not confirm the numbers.

North Korea has made rapid progress in its ballistic missile and nuclear programmes in recent years, as it demands international recognition as a legitimate nuclear state.

North Korea has conducted multiple long-range missile tests since 2017, the year it last tested a nuclear weapon . In a report submitted to the UN security council in 2020, international experts said the North had “probably developed nuclear devices to fit into the warheads of its ballistic missiles”.
sources.headline: North Korea has built new uranium facility to expand nuclear arsenal, UN agency says

stories.headline: Philippines ferry fire kills at least five as search continues for dozens missing

sources.body:
At least five people have died and 86 are missing after a fire broke out on a ferry in the Philippines, the country's coastguard said.

The MV June Aster, which set off from Manila ferrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members, was nearing its destination at the tourist hotspot of Coron when it caught fire.

The blaze, which erupted at 18:45 local time (10:45 GMT) Wednesday, was still burning as of 11:00 on Thursday. The strong currents and thick smoke were a challenge to those working to extinguish it, the coastguard said.

A survivor says he was in the sea for two hours before he got rescued. "It was cold. If the rescue was delayed, I would definitely have died," Roland Lerma told the BBC.

Video clips shared by the coastguard on Wednesday night showed the vessel engulfed in flames and people being pulled out of the water into rescue boats.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation, the coastguard said.

The coastguard said preliminary interviews with the survivors suggest the fire started in the cargo hold, which is the compartment where containers and or goods are stored, the coastguard said. Some passengers were not wearing life vests, they noted.

Forty-three people have been rescued but it is unclear how many have sustained injuries.

Seven of the survivors were taken to a hospital in Culion, a larger neighbouring island, which has higher bed capacity and more comprehensive healthcare services.

A first responder told the BBC they had never seen such a disaster in Coron, calling it "really heartbreaking".

"I was one of the people who carried and transported the casualties to the hospital last night," they said, adding that the ferry was an hour away from its destination.

The survivors were taken to an evacuation centre in Barangay Turda, which sits just north of Marcilla. The state of their injuries is unclear.

Anelyn Magbanua is among those anxiously waiting for news of their loved ones.

Her husband Marlon had spent a few days in Manila visiting their two children, who were going to school in the capital city.

Magbanua last heard from him while the ferry was passing through a village about two hours from the port in Coron, she tells the BBC.

"I was expecting that the ferry will arrive at the pier at between 18:00 and 19:00 yesterday," she said, adding that she had gone to bed early but was awakened by a cousin who told her the ferry Marlon was on had caught fire.

"I couldn't describe what I am feeling right now. I have been crying and praying since last night," Magbanua says.

She'd travelled to a hospital in Coron, hoping to find Marlon among the survivors – but he remains unaccounted for.

"My two-year-old son and I are outside the hospital as we speak. We have nothing but ourselves," she says.

Rai Garcia has three family friends among those missing.

Mae Lorraine Galera-Navoa, who is the sister of Garcia's brother-in-law, had travelled to Luzon to attend her father's funeral, accompanied by her husband Elyzer Navoa and their three-year-old daughter Hiraya Joy.

They had been travelling home to El Nido in Palawan on board the vessel when it caught fire.
sources.headline: Five dead and 86 missing as 'heartbreaking' fire breaks out on Philippines ferry

sources.body:
Multiple search and rescue vessels deployed after blaze off Palawan island leaves at least five dead, says coast guard

A large-scale ⁠search and rescue operation ​is under way off the western Philippine island of Palawan on Thursday after a passenger ferry caught fire, killing five people and leaving ⁠scores of passengers missing.

The Philippine coast guard said multiple vessels and other assets were searching for survivors as rescue teams used drift-modelling tools ⁠to identify areas where people may have been carried by currents.

Based on the vessel’s manifest, the ​number of survivors – currently at 43 – and ‌the fatalities reported so ‌far, authorities estimated that more than 80 people remained unaccounted for, although the figures could still change.

Coast ‌guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said rescuers could not yet enter the M/V June Aster, with the search hampered by thick smoke still billowing from the ferry and concerns about extreme heat and the risk of explosions.

Drone footage released by the coast guard showed the blackened ferry surrounded by clear blue-green waters, with the vessel still generating smoke hours after the ‌fire broke out on Wednesday night.

Cayabyab said the vessel’s manifest listed a total of 117 passengers and 17 crew members. The ferry had departed from Baseco ​in Manila and was bound for Coron, a popular tourist destination in Palawan known for its diving sites, beaches and island-hopping attractions.

Among the 43 people rescued were two Chilean nationals, said Aileen Ausente, a spokesperson for the coast guard in Palawan, adding that air assets were on standby to help with rescue operations, ⁠weather permitting.

The burned ferry had drifted farther from its original location overnight, ​carried by currents and winds, ​adding to the challenges facing rescuers, ​Cayabyab said.

The cause of the fire is under investigation.

Ferry travel is a ​common mode of ‌transport in the Philippines , ​an archipelago of ​more than 7,600 islands, where millions of people rely on boats to travel between provinces.

The country has a patchy maritime safety record, and many previous ferry disasters have been linked to overcrowding, rough weather and lax enforcement of safety regulations.
sources.headline: Deadly Philippines ferry fire triggers search for scores of missing

sources.body: At least five people died and dozens were unaccounted for Thursday after a ferry caught fire off the Philippine island province of Palawan, with 43 passengers and crew rescued so far. Coast guard teams continued search and rescue operations as officials worked to establish what happened.
sources.headline: Deadly Philippines ferry fire leaves dozens missing

stories.headline: Russian attacks kill seven in Ukraine as Kyiv strikes Arctic gas facilities

sources.body:
Ukraine launches one of its deepest strikes to date, targeting gas plants in Russia’s Arctic region.

Ukrainian drones strike Russian Caspian Sea port in Dagestan

Russian forces have launched attacks across Ukraine, killing at least seven people, according to Ukrainian officials, as Kyiv claimed responsibility for a drone attack that set off a fire at a natural gas plant deep in Russia’s Arctic region.

Four people were killed in a Russian attack in Mykolaiv in southern Ukraine overnight on Thursday, while three were killed in a drone attack on a shopping centre in the northeastern city of Sumy, according to Ukrainian authorities.

Heorhii ⁠Reshetilov, the acting governor of the Mykolaiv region, said the Russian strikes there hit both civilian and industrial infrastructure, killing two men and two women. At least 19 others were wounded, he said on Telegram.

The attack in Sumy left at least 14 people wounded, according to Oleh Hryhorov, head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration. Three of the victims were children, he said on Telegram.

The Russian Ministry of Defence confirmed the attack in Mykolaiv, but said it targeted a drone warehouse. The ministry said it also hit the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk and two vessels near Odesa on the Black Sea.

The targets of the strikes were being used for military purposes, the ministry claimed.

The attacks came after Russian authorities said Ukrainian forces had launched a drone attack on the country’s Yamal-Nenets region, which is located some 2,800 kilometres (1,700 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

Dmitry Artyukhov, the region’s governor, said the attack targeted an industrial facility in Novy Urengoy. The attack was repelled, but falling debris from the drone caused a fire, he said on Telegram.

“The main thing is that there were no deaths or injuries. The extent and nature of the damage are being determined,” he added.

Artem Zhoga, the Kremlin’s envoy to the Urals, said Wednesday’s strike was the first ever to hit the Arctic part of the region.

Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces (SOF) confirmed the attack in a series of posts on X.

“For the first time! Deepest strike of the war: Ukrainian SOF hit critical russian plants more than 3,000 km away,” it said. “Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces carried out the deepest strike inside russia since the beginning of the full-scale war.”

In the posts, the Ukrainian force claimed it “successfully struck” two gas plants, Novy Urengoy and Purovsky.

“Until today, the area was considered a safe rear zone for the aggressor,” it added.

The Ukrainian force said the facilities play a key role in Russia’s gas industry, processing large volumes of condensate from gas fields across the Yamal region, processing millions of tonnes of condensate per year.

Gazprom used ⁠to export gas from Yamal as far as Western Europe ⁠until relations broke ⁠down following the start of Russia’s war in Ukraine in 2022.

It estimated the region’s gas resources at ‌26.5 trillion cubic metres as of 2020, enough to cover global demand for more than ‌six ‌years.
sources.headline: Russian attacks kill 7 in Ukraine as Kyiv targets gas plants deep in Arctic

stories.headline: Trump promises $5,000 payments to every adult American if Republicans retain Congress

sources.body:
US President Donald Trump says he would offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress in November's midterm elections – a plan that would cost more than a trillion dollars.

The offer was made in a speech at the party's first-ever convention in the middle of a US presidential term.

He gave no details on how it would work or be funded – saying only that the money would have to be spent in the US. Vice-President JD Vance has linked the plan to the revenue that Trump has raised for the US government using tariffs.

The plan has proven controversial. Democrats labelled it an "empty promise" and others questioned whether such a pledge was legal.

It may be the first time a US president offered such a payout to Americans, in the context of an election year plea to get out and vote.

Whether the plan would be possible or not appeared to be beside the point. The idea drew raucous applause at the convention and Trump seemed to relish the moment.

There are nearly 270 million American adults, meaning a $5,000 payout would cost the US government some $1.3 trillion.

Questions have begun to be raised about whether his plan is feasible – especially as prices rise in the US, partially as a result of the war that the US and Israel started with Iran in February.

Iran's retaliation has included attacks against US bases and allies in the Gulf – but crucially it has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to transit.

The blockage has caused fluctuations in oil prices worldwide and Trump has faced pressure from his party to end the war.

On Wednesday, the US president warned his supporters that the war would not end until after the midterms and that oil prices would not come down until then.

He made the comments ahead of his speech in Texas, repeating it at the convention where he argued that short-term economic pain was worth it to prevent Tehran from developing nuclear weapons.

Trump's long speech at the Republican convention in Dallas, Texas, touched on the core of the conflict – the impact on Americans' standard of living. His pledge to increase their spending power drew raucous applause in the hall.

"If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them," Trump said, "I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000."

"We don't want you going to Canada to spend the money," he said.

"We don't want you going to China, to Germany. You got to spend the money in the United States of America." It is not clear how the spending would be monitored.

The BBC has asked the White House for further clarification on how Trump's plan would work.

It is not the first time that Trump promised such payouts – he has previously proposed $2,000 cheques to be funded by tariff revenues.

Vice-President JD Vance indicated that these post-election payments could similarly be made possible by the money Trump has raised using his wide-ranging tariff programme.
sources.headline: Trump says every adult American would get $5,000 if Republicans win midterms

stories.headline: Republicans confront cost-of-living and oil-price pressures at their midterm convention

sources.body: DALLAS — Republicans are panicking that President Donald Trump's policies are drowning out their cost-of-living message — and that it may be too close to the election to fix it. GOP lawmakers and candidates woke up in Texas on Wednesday to an alarming reality: Trump deepening his trade war with Canada as oil hit $100 per barrel , following new military strikes against Iran. Publicly, Republicans plan to downplay their latest woes — or blame the Democrats. But several of them at the midterm convention this week are privately strategizing with GOP leaders and Trump administration officials to shore up vulnerable candidates in battlegrounds and in states the president won by double digits in 2024. Vice President JD Vance is scheduled to address a breakfast Thursday with the delegations from Pennsylvania, Ohio, Michigan and Wisconsin, where Republicans are eager to hear how he will navigate the party’s economic woes, according to three people with direct knowledge of the matter, granted anonymity to share private plans. Others are pushing to use the convention to reclaim the cost of living issue that’s haunting Republicans after it buoyed them two years ago, planning to argue in their speeches that their party can still be trusted to bring down prices. In a closed-door meeting Wednesday, a group of top senators and candidates in tough races — including Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio), North Carolina Senate nominee Michael Whatley and Georgia Republican Senate nominee Rep. Mike Collins — huddled with leaders from the Senate GOP-aligned super PAC to discuss a battleground map increasingly under pressure as the party tries to fend off voters’ ire around the economy. “You can’t hide the fact of what the price of gasoline is, we know that,” Collins told POLITICO in an interview after the closed-door meeting, as he reiterated his support for Trump’s efforts to neutralize Iran as a nuclear threat, arguing that the U.S. has long been at war with Iran but “we’re putting an end to it with this president.” Many Republicans didn’t want to talk about economic concerns amid the party at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, where MAGA hats cost $47 (a discount from the $55 online ) and water went for $8 a bottle. “We are going the wrong direction,” said one GOP lawmaker attending the convention granted anonymity, like others in this story, to speak candidly of the spiraling economic indicators and the challenges they were creating. “We don’t have a lot of time left.” Senior Republicans are quietly dismayed about the pileup of Trump economic moves that have rattled voters and key industries in their states — including the worsening trade war with Canada that threatens the auto and farm sectors in the Midwest, his step to import more foreign beef ahead of the midterms that’s infuriated ranchers and farmers from Texas to Iowa, along with spiking oil prices amid the war in Iran that are cutting across the map. “We’re putting Iowa in play,” one frustrated senior House Republican said on the sidelines of the convention of the Senate map. “We’re putting Texas in play. They shouldn’t be.” The one advantage they have: money. Battleground Republicans and GOP leaders have been itching for Trump to unleash his massive war chest to help them fend off Democratic attacks over voters’ concerns about gas and everyday costs among the ongoing war. Trump’s orbit started to make good on its promises Wednesday morning, doling out millions in spending for key Senate races through an affiliated Super PAC known as No Going Back PAC Inc., two people with direct knowledge of the matter confirmed. But Republicans know that campaign funds can’t solve everything. “We got to talk about the issues that people are dealing with. Families can't afford their house, they can't afford the food, they can't afford health care, they can't afford child care,” Sen. Rick Scott (R-Fla.) said in an interview in the convention hall. He placed most of the onus on Congress to tackle those issues and cut spending, but admitted Trump’s war with Iran had economic consequences. “We have higher gas prices now as a result of the president trying to keep us safe as a result of what Iran wants to do,” Scott said. “So that's hopefully a short-term problem that he's going to deal with by destroying the regime.” In a statement, White House spokesperson Olivia Wales argued that Democrats “created the affordability crisis.” “President Trump has spent every day in office working to undo their mess and lower costs for working families by signing the largest middle class tax cuts in history, lowering the cost of prescription drugs, permanently expanding the child tax credit, fueling wage growth, and reshoring American manufacturing to create more high paying jobs,” Wales said. Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the RNC, similarly blamed Democrats for surging prices, adding that “Republicans are cutting taxes, lowering drug prices, and putting money back in families’ pockets.” Several Republicans plan to use their convention addresses to blame their Democratic opponents for voters’ price pains and argue it’s Republicans who are putting more money in Americans’ pockets — like Mike LiPetri, who’s running to unseat Democratic Rep. Tom Suozzi in New York. Others plan to paint a rosier picture of the economy than many voters say is the case right now. That’s been a hard message for Republicans to sell. An August POLITICO Poll shows that a 34% plurality of Americans hold Trump fully responsible for the state of the current U.S. economy, compared with just 17% who say the same for former President Joe Biden. And the very real time crunch — with less than two months until the November election — was a tangible pressure throughout the day in Dallas, as Republican lawmakers, battleground candidates and party officials gathered for what was planned to be a grand event to celebrate GOP accomplishments and drive turnout. “Look, I think obviously we want to continue to drive down costs, whether it's energy, whether it is housing, whether it is groceries,” Rep. Mike Lawler (R-N.Y.), one of the most at-risk House Republicans in November, said in an interview. “We're seeing, you know, obviously continued volatility in the oil markets, and we want to bring that down.” Lawler, who is speaking at the convention Thursday night, touted Trump’s deal over Venezuela oil and largely blamed policy moves by New York Democrats for his state’s higher energy costs. Trump told reporters Wednesday that oil prices are set to drop amid the ongoing U.S. conflict with Iran — but not until after the midterms, which is much later than those anxious Republicans would hope. Some GOP hopefuls point to the overall goal to dismantle Iran’s nuclear capabilities as a necessary national security posture. The uptick in oil prices, therefore, is a short-term consequence for a greater long-term foreign policy success. “We [have] to be patient with the fluctuations, especially with oil and what's happening in the Gulf now,” said Marty O’Donnell, the Republican looking to unseat Democratic Rep. Susie Lee from her Las Vegas seat. And the Republicans assembled in Dallas were the ones most likely to support the president — plenty of other lawmakers, including members running in tough races, stayed away, as did some rank-and-file Republicans. “We have to hope that in six weeks the price per barrel goes down because it's a big deal,” said one Georgia-based Republican strategist who is not attending the Dallas convention. “The Dems have been beating the daylights out of us on that for a while now.” A GOP county chair in a region with House races that have been made more competitive by Trump’s unpopularity echoed those concerns. “There's no other commodity that when you drive down the street, you see the price,” said the county chair who also wasn’t in Dallas. “I know what gas costs because it's on a fucking billboard on every intersection, and I'm forced to see it. It's the most visible indicator of the economy, where we stand.” And while Republicans are hoping that Trump can get his party’s economic messaging on track in his convention keynote address, some aren’t holding their breath for a major breakthrough. “Maybe, maybe, maybe, maybe, maybe the president delivers a coherent speech that is clear, that is direct, that is policy oriented, that is forward-looking, and they can cut that up in social media and post that up all over the place,” said the GOP county chair. “Will he do that? Absolutely not.” Mia McCarthy contributed to this report.
sources.headline: ‘We are going in the wrong direction’: Republican convention dogged by the cost of living

Former CVS executive Helena Foulkes defeats Rhode Island Governor Dan McKee in Democratic primary

sources.body: Rhode Island Democratic Gov. Dan McKee became the first governor in eight years in the U.S. to lose a primary, falling on Wednesday to former CVS executive Helena Foulkes and becoming the latest victim of a rough year for incumbents. McKee’s campaign was bogged down by the botched handling of a years-long project to rebuild the Washington Bridge, which transports more than 70,000 drivers through Providence each day. The project has suffered from delays, cost overruns and disputes between state officials and former contractors that have raised questions about transparency and accountability for the project. Foulkes spent much of the primary hammering McKee over his handling of the bridge project — a strategy that ultimately proved successful. McKee had partially closed the bridge in 2023, and estimated at the time that it would fully reopen this summer. But last year, he said the bridge likely won’t be completed until 2028. Construction began in June. Throughout his campaign, McKee continued to insist that the bridge project was handled well. He told The New York Times in August that “people are going to realize we did the right thing.” The last incumbent governor to lose a primary was Kansas Gov. Jeff Colyer in 2018. McKee’s loss Wednesday adds to the substantial list of Democratic incumbents ousted in primary challenges , though this race didn’t feature the same generational and ideological contrasts as other primaries that have felled Democrats this cycle. Foulkes and McKee, both baby boomers, both ran center-left campaigns. Foulkes’ victory adds a chapter to her family’s long political lineage. Her grandfather, Thomas J. Dodd, and her uncle, Chris Dodd, were both senators from Connecticut. She worked as an executive at CVS for over 25 years before launching a 2022 run for governor. McKee won that round, but she got the final word on Wednesday.
sources.headline: Dan McKee becomes first governor in 8 years to lose primary

El Centro Nacional de Inteligencia (CNI) mantuvo el 29 de julio, víspera de la entrada masiva en Ceuta, comunicaciones con la Delegación del Gobierno y la Guardia Civil en las que trasladaba su preocupación por las convocatorias surgidas en redes sociales para el día siguiente, 30 de julio, y por la posibilidad de un "asalto" por "mar y tierra" en la ciudad autónoma. "Hay dos grupos diferentes con un total de 180.000 seguidores. Para q te hagas a la idea del alcance de la difusión", comenta textualmente.

El texto está incluido entre las comunicaciones entre el CNI y el gabinete de la Delegación del Gobierno en Ceuta por Whatsapp. Se envió el 29 de julio a las 13.52 . Alertaba de mensajes en redes sociales que se estaban multiplicando, en grupos con unos 180.000 seguidores, llamando a un asalto a las 20 horas del día 30 de julio "aprovechando fiesta del trono y q sus FCS estarán liados", en referencia a los cuerpos policiales marroquíes.

Ese mismo día figura otra comunicación entre el CNI y la Guardia Civil, una llamada a las 13.53 horas . "Tenemos información de un intento de entradas a nado y salto a la valla para mañana, día de la Fiesta del Trono", se transcribe en el texto. "Tenemos varios grupos en Fb y WhatsApp incentivando estas entradas", se añade.

Del 29 de julio también figura una nota del CNI dirigida a los servicios de inteligencia interior y exterior marroquíes (DGST y DGED) en los que les alerta de este intento de asalto, de la existencia de grupos de Whatsapp con nombre "Asalto a la valla", también grupos de Facebook con 160.000 y 22.000 participantes , donde se indica que la Fiesta del Trono es "una última oportunidad" para cruzar a Ceuta.

Fuentes del CNI han querido "aclarar" tras la desclasificación que, pese a hacerse eco de la información sobre la citada "campaña" en redes sociales, el organismo "no anticipó la magnitud y naturaleza de lo que terminó ocurriendo el día 30, al ser un fenómeno inusual que no se corresponde con las crisis migratorias conocidas hasta la fecha".

A la Fiesta del Trono y la posible "relajación" de las fuerzas policiales marroquíes también hace referencia otro documento previo, del 28 de julio, un día antes que el CNI. Lo realiza el CENIF de la Policía Nacional , un documento para su "difusión interna" que alerta de la repercusión de la sentencia del Tribunal Supremo sobre la ley de extranjería y las devoluciones a quien entre a nado en España.

Asegura que va creciendo ligeramente en redes sociales el ofrecimiento, por ejemplo, de trajes de neopreno para cruzar —se incluyen fotografías—, y advierte de que los "indicios observados podrían constituir una señal temprana de un cambio de comportamiento que conviene seguir monitorizando". Añade que es una tendencia "incipiente", pero que la entrada a nado en Ceuta "constituye la modalidad de mayor riesgo e incidencia relativa ".

Sin embargo, al día siguiente, el 29 de julio, el mismo CENIF alerta de "RIESGO MUY ALTO", en mayúsculas, de entradas a nado. Se trata de un informe de nuevo de "difusión interna" en el que se asegura que "las entradas a nado constituyen la principal amenaza actual en Ceuta, un total de 921 cruces a nado durante el último mes y cientos de personas rescatadas por Marruecos y España. El perfil predominante corresponde, casi en su totalidad, a individuos jóvenes marroquís", explica.

Joaquín Vera, Carlota Guindal, Asier Martiarena

El Centro Nacional de Inteligencia (CNI) avisó horas antes de iniciarse la entrada masiva de migrantes a Ceuta de un “llamamiento” para cruzar a nado o a pie el espigón fronterizo del Tarajal. Los servicios secretos lanzaron este aviso por WhatsApp a la Delegación del Gobierno en la ciudad autónoma y a la Guardia Civil. Lo hicieron en torno a las 14.00 horas del día anterior. Esa misma tarde, el CNI también envió una “nota urgente” a Marruecos para avisar de la existencia de un plan para entrar el día 30 promovido en redes sociales. Sin embargo, de la documentación desclasificada este miércoles por el Gobierno no se refleja que se calibrara la magnitud de lo que iba a ocurrir: un asalto a la valla, por el que entraron en apenas 48 horas más de 80.000 personas. Y tampoco aparece que estas alertas fuesen elevadas a instancias superiores para actuar, aunque fuese con poco margen.

El CNI no fue el único que detectó estos movimientos. Tanto la Policía Nacional como la Guardia Civil habían estado emitiendo informes internos desde días antes sobre el riesgo de un aumento de entradas a raíz de la sentencia del Tribunal Supremo, del 8 de julio, que prohibía el rechazo en frontera –es decir, devolución sin tramitación administrativa– para los migrantes que lograban entrar a Ceuta a nado. En la medida en que fueron avanzando los días y las alertas seguían, en los informes se incluyeron los movimientos detectados a través de redes sociales y grupos de mensajería instantánea. Incluso se llegó a detectar un incremento de las ventas de neoprenos para lanzarse al mar. Justo las jornadas previas, las entradas se dispararon y así se hizo constar en diversos informes. Se aconsejó refuerzos en la frontera e incluso colaboración a Marruecos, pero de la documentación ahora conocida se desprende que no se previó tal avalancha. Solo el día 30, ya con miles de personas entrando a la vez, en los informes se habla de “riesgo extremo de colapso” o “desborde” de la situación.

Joaquín Vera, Carlota Guindal, Asier Martiarena

El presidente del Gobierno decidió desclasificar estos documentos por la crisis política en la que desembocó el choque de posiciones entre el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, quien aseguró que no hubo alertas de la entrada masiva, y la titular de Defensa, Margarita Robles, que siempre ha defendido a capa y espada la labor del CNI en este asunto.

Una vez conocidos los papeles, que con toda probabilidad acabarán en la causa abierta en la Audiencia Nacional, las interpretaciones siguen siendo dispares. ¿Hubo o no hubo alertas?; ¿se actuó o no se actuó ante estas?; ¿se calibró o no la magnitud de las entradas? Es esa la lectura política, pero también tendrá una lectura judicial.

Además de la diferencia de criterios entre ambos ministerios, otro punto nuclear es el papel de Marruecos en todo esto. Las interpretaciones también son dispares. Los papeles desclasificados revelan que el CNI puso en conocimiento lo que sabía el día 29 de los llamamientos a una entrada a Ceuta. La Guardia Civil se inclinaba por la tesis de que Marruecos colaboraba, mientras que la Policía Nacional señalaba al reino alauita como una amenaza por un ánimo de pretender demostrar públicamente la dependencia y debilidad de España.

sources.body: <p>Pedro Sánchez ha dejado muy claro que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-09/el-gobierno-se-revuelve-contra-una-nueva-provocacion-del-supremo-ahora-con-la-ley-de-nietos.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-09/el-gobierno-se-revuelve-contra-una-nueva-provocacion-del-supremo-ahora-con-la-ley-de-nietos.html">el Gobierno está muy molesto con la decisión del Tribunal Supremo</a> de suspender cautelarmente la inclusión en el censo electoral, y por tanto el derecho a voto, de miles de nuevos españoles que han logrado la nacionalidad a través de la llamada <i>ley de nietos</i>. En una entrevista en TVE, el presidente ha cargado sobre todo contra Vox y el PP, por sus ataques a la norma, pero también en el bloque estaba el Tribunal Supremo indirectamente. “No estamos a favor ni compartimos la decisión del Supremo, y les hemos pedido que resuelvan cuanto antes porque estamos hablando de derechos fundamentales”, ha dicho Sánchez. Pero justo antes, y hablando del PP y Vox, el presidente ha lanzado la idea de que detrás de este ataque a la ley hay “una corriente de fondo de la ultraderecha en todo el mundo, a la que se suma el PP, en la que cuestionan la democracia y hablan de pucherazos. Aún me acuerdo de cuando dijeron que habíamos bloqueado unos trenes desde Valencia para impedir el voto en las últimas elecciones, como si en los trenes solo viajaran votantes del PP”, ha sentenciado. La tesis de Sánchez es que en el trasfondo de esta polémica contra la <i>ley de nietos</i>, que no se produjo cuando se aprobó y se empezó a aplicar en 2022, está la idea de cuestionar el proceso electoral, como sucedió con las dudas sobre el voto por correo y otras cuestiones. “Esta ley lleva en vigor desde 2022, y en 2023 el PP ganó en el voto exterior y logró alterar el resultado en favor del PP; ganó un escaño en 2023. La posición de la Junta Electoral era favorable. Hoy el PP cambia de posición. Y es por esta corriente de fondo, este cuestionamiento por parte de la ultraderecha de los regímenes democráticos”, ha insistido.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-09/sanchez-acusa-a-la-derecha-de-cuestionar-la-democracia-al-ir-contra-la-ley-de-nietos-y-pide-al-supremo-que-decida-rapido.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

El Tribunal Supremo ha decido suspender de manera cautelar la inscripción en el Censo Electoral de Residentes Ausentes (CERA) de las personas que obtuvieron la nacionalidad española a raíz de la Ley de Memoria Democrática, popularmente conocida como 'ley de nietos', salvo que acrediten su condición de descendientes de españoles que sufrieron exilio por la Guerra Civil y la dictadura franquista.

Mediante una decisión a la que ha tenido acceso RTVE, la Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo acuerda suspender la posibilidad de inscribirse en el censo y votar a estas personas en los sucesivos procesos electorales que puedan convocarse, estimando parcialmente las medidas cautelares pedidas por Vox e Iustitia Europa. Te explicamos el origen de esta decisión y sus consecuencias.

La llamada ' ley de nietos' es el nombre con el que se conoce una disposición adicional de la Ley de Memoria Democrática . Permite obtener la nacionalidad a los nacidos fuera de España de padres o abuelos españoles que la perdieron tras sufrir exilio por "razones políticas, ideológicas o de creencia o de orientación e identidad sexual ". También, los hijos nacidos en el exterior de mujeres españolas "que perdieron su nacionalidad por casarse con extranjeros antes de la entrada en vigor de la Constitución de 1978".

Tras la ley, el Gobierno dictó una instrucción sobre cómo aplicar esta medida en los registros consulares, los encargados de los trámites. En este texto, señaló que "se presumirá la condición de exiliado " a todos los que "salieron de España entre el 18 de julio de 1936 y el 31 de diciembre de 1955 ", con la condición de que acrediten esa "salida del territorio español". Es decir, amplió la consideración de exiliados y en esto se apoyan los recurrentes para interpretar que la norma abre la puerta a la obtención generalizada de la nacionalidad y, por tanto, el derecho al voto.

El Supremo suspende la inscripción en el censo de votantes del exterior (CERA) a quienes se acojan a esta denominada ‘ley de nietos’, tanto las que ya están tramitadas como las que están en proceso. No suspende la obtención de la nacionalidad, sino la posibilidad de votar.

Lo que exige el alto tribunal es que se acredite que se logra la nacionalidad española de acuerdo con las exigencias de la ley , "sin haber aplicado la presunción" que se dictó después, la citada instrucción. Es necesario acreditar haber nacido "fuera de España, de padre o madre, abuelo o abuela que originariamente fueran españoles, y que hubieran sufrido exilio por razones políticas, ideológicas, o de creencia o de orientación de identidad sexual (…)".

El Supremo ordena por ello a la Junta Electoral Central (JEC) que requiera de inmediato sobre ese extremo a los encargados de los registros consulares. Igualmente, ordena a la Oficina de Censo Electoral que proceda al desglose de los expedientes de inscripción censal que procedan de la aplicación directa de los supuestos de exilio recogidos en la ley, y de los aprobados al amparo de la interpretación realizada por la instrucción.

"></img><p>Cambios profundos en el Departamento de Interior de Cataluña. sources.body:
Aquest dimecres s'ha conegut la renúncia de Josep Lluís Trapero a continuar com a director general dels Mossos d'Esquadra , però els motius, a banda que ha estat " una decisió personal ", no han transcendit.

Ho ha dit la consellera d'Interior, Núria Parlon , que ha dit que ella volia que continués en el càrrec fins a final de mandat, i ha afegit que li ha insistit perquè canviés d'opinió, sense èxit.

Però ha estat significatiu que Parlon hagi confirmat la dimissió de Trapero en una compareixença en què no ha participat el mateix Trapero, cosa que ha suggerit que no ha estat un comiat gaire amistós.

En tot cas, tant el dimissionari Trapero com el seu entorn personal mantenen un silenci rigorós i no han donat cap mena de detall ni explicació del perquè de la decisió.

Fonts consultades per 3CatInfo han apuntat que hi ha hagut diversos motius per dimitir, i el detonant hauria estat el relleu al capdavant de la Secretaria General d'Interior i Seguretat Pública .

Fins fa pocs dies aquest càrrec, que es considera el número 2 d'Interior , l'ocupava Tomàs Carrión , que ha decidit plegar, i l'ha substituït Joana Ricardo , que era directora general d'Administració de Seguretat.

Segons les fonts consultades, Trapero i Ricardo haurien tingut diferències i desavinences considerables els últims dos anys dins de la conselleria, i l' ascens de la segona hauria afegit tensió a la situació.

També apunten que el relleu de Miquel Esquius al capdavant de la direcció policial dels Mossos per la fins ara cap de la regió de Girona, Sílvia Catà, tampoc hauria agradat gens a Trapero.

Aquests dos relleus haurien estat la gota que ha fet vessar el got, però també haurien tingut importància en la decisió les polèmiques que els últims mesos han envoltat els Mossos, sobretot en l'àmbit escolar.

Principalment, la infiltració d'agents policials en una assemblea de mestres enmig de les vagues del sector, però també el pla de destinar agents dels Mossos als centres escolars per fer de mediadors.

Tant la infiltració com el pla van provocar una allau de crítiques des de la comunitat educativa, i malgrat la dimissió de Trapero, els sindicats ja han dit que no renuncien a actuar judicialment contra la infiltració.

I malgrat que la renúncia de Trapero ha estat una sorpresa per a tothom, Parlon ja tenia el relleu preparat: serà Ferran López , que el 2017 ja es va encarregar de la direcció política dels Mossos.

Va ser quan el govern de Mariano Rajoy va aplicar l'article 155 de la Constitució, va agafar el control del govern de la Generalitat, va dissoldre el Parlament i, també, va destituir Trapero del càrrec del qual ara ha dimitit.

Aquest dijous, la consellera d'Interior, Núria Parlon , ha rebutjat que la dimissió de Josep Lluís Trapero com a director general dels Mossos d'Esquadra hagi estat causada per desavinences entre els dos. Hi ha insistit en una entrevista a "El matí de Catalunya Ràdio":

A mi ningú m'ha sentit mai dir res dolent del director general de la policia.

Parlon ha demanat que no s'alimentin més les polèmiques sobre els motius de la marxa de Trapero, a qui ha qualificat d' "excel·lent professional" . També ha destacat la bona feina feta durant els dos últims anys, que ha permès posar el cos policial "en un bon moment".

stories.headline: Catalonia records 556 deaths by suicide or self-harm in 2025 despite a three-year decline

sources.body: Catalunya encadena tres anys consecutius de reducció de la mortalitat per suïcidi o autolesió , tot i que el nombre de defuncions indica que aquestes conductes continuen sent un greu problema de salut pública . Així, durant l’any 2025 es van registrar 556 defuncions per suïcidi o autolesió entre persones residents a Catalunya, segons dades provisionals publicades per l’Institut Nacional d’Estadística. Aquesta xifra significa una reducció del 17 % de la mortalitat per suïcidi respecte a la taxa de defuncions des del 2022. També et pot interessar L’Ajuntament de Barcelona presenta un pla per a la prevenció del suïcidi: “Volem trencar el tabú” Jordi Escofet 2 minuts de lectura Més suïcidis en homes que en dones Els homes continuen marcant una mortalitat clarament més alta que les dones: 413 suïcidis corresponen a homes i 143, a dones . En aquest sentit, el grup demogràfic en homes amb una mortalitat més alta són els majors de 85 anys , amb 31 defuncions per suïcidi. En dones , el grup de 50 a 59 anys , amb 39 suïcidis, i les majors de 85 anys, amb set morts, és on hi ha una una taxa de mortalitat més alta per aquesta causa. La taxa de defuncions no és tampoc homogènia en tots els grups de població. Les dades mostren increments en alguns grups d’edat, especialment en dones d’entre 40 i 59 anys i homes d’entre 55 i 74 anys. Finalitza el primer pla de prevenció Aquest descens de l’evolució dels suïcidis a Catalunya coincideix amb la finalització del primer Pla de prevenció del suïcidi , desplegat entre 2021 i 2025 pel Departament de Salut. Durant aquests anys, la taxa de mortalitat va passar de 9,27 morts per 100.000 habitants el 2022 a 9,20 defuncions el 2023, 7,91 el 2024 i 7,68 morts l’any 2025. En aquest desplegament, la Generalitat ha impulsat més de 150 actuacions en diferents àmbits , com el sanitari, l’educatiu o el comunitari. En aquest mateix marc, Salut ha creat l’Observatori de Prevenció del Suïcidi de Catalunya i la Taula de de Salut Mental , que ha atès més de 77.000 consultes en quatre anys al telèfon 061 Salut Respon. Per tot plegat, la conselleria considera que la prevenció del suïcidi és una prioritat i ja està elaborant un segon pla per als propers anys. Una xifra que suposa una mitjana de 52 consultes diàries . Durant la trucada, els professionals analitzen si hi ha perill imminent de risc per a la vida de la persona, donen consells i fan contenció telefònica. Per tot això, en un 64 % d’aquestes consultes es va requerir l’activació d’una ambulància del SEM. Amb dades recollides entre el juny del 2022 i el juny del 2026 , la franja prevalent en les consultes al 061 Salut Respon va ser la de joves de 20 a 29 anys , seguida de la franja de 40 a 49 anys. Del conjunt, el 85 % de les persones ateses ja tenien un diagnòstic previ d’algun trastorn de salut mental. sources.body:
Les conductes suïcides -idea de suïcidar-se i temptatives de suïcidi- van a a l’alça a Barcelona , segons ha informat aquest dimecres l’Ajuntament. És així des del 2021, especialment entre els joves, “coincidint amb l’empitjorament de la salut mental observat a conseqüència de la crisi social i econòmica derivada de la pandèmia de COVID-19”, explica el consistori en un comunicat .

El 2019, abans la pandèmia , es van registrar 527 episodis d’ideació suïcida (pensar, considerar o planificar un suïcidi), i 577 de temptativa en residents a la ciutat. Cinc anys després, el 2024, les conductes suïcides eren força més altes, amb 1.128 episodis d’ideació i 860 de temptativa suïcida. En canvi, les morts per suïcidi s’han mantingut estables els darrers anys, amb 117 persones el 2023.

Aquestes dades estan desglossades i explicades en l’informe La Conducta Suïcida a Barcelona 2024 , que descriu per primera vegada les ideacions, temptatives i suïcidis a la ciutat, així com la seva evolució en el període 2017-2024.

Segons l’Ajuntament, les ideacions i les temptatives són més freqüents en dones i persones joves, mentre que els suïcidis es concentren principalment en homes i persones de més edat. De fet, els suïcidis són la causa principal de mort prematura ens homes a la ciutat. Les dades mostren que  la conducta suïcida és un “fenomen complex i heterogeni”: les ideacions, les temptatives i els suïcidis presenten patrons i factors associats diferents, i, en conseqüència, requereixen estratègies específiques de prevenció i intervenció, diferenciades però coordinades.

La regidora de Salut de l’Ajuntament, Marta Villanueva , ha presentat aquest dimecres l’Estratègia de Prevenció de la Conducta Suïcida 2026-2032 . Inicialment, es desplegaran quaranta-quatre accions fins al 2028. Entre les actuacions previstes, s’elaborarà un mapa dels punts de risc a l’espai públic per valorar la implantació de mesures preventives, com ara barreres físiques o la senyalització de recursos de suport i ajuda.

D’altra banda, l’estratègia inclou la implementació d’un protocol d’intervenció en situacions de desnonaments amb risc de suïcidis , adreçat als professionals que hi intervenen. El juliol del 2024, dues dones es van suïcidar al carrer de las Navas de Tolosa abans de ser desnonades . I en l’àmbit educatiu, es farà formació sobre conducta autolítica als docents dels centres educatius.

Entre el 2020 i l’agost de 2026, el Telèfon de Prevenció del Suïcidi ha atès més de 32.000 trucades, i entre el 2022 i l’agost de 2026 el Xat de Suport Emocional per a Joves ha gestionat gairebé 27.000 converses. Més de 3.500 professionals han rebut formació en prevenció de la conducta suïcida.

stories.headline: Catalan doctors announce an indefinite strike beginning in October

sources.body:
Metges de Catalunya (MC) ha anunciat la convocatòria d'una vaga indefinida a partir de mitjans d'octubre, amb la data d'inici encara per concretar.

Així ho han acordat juntament amb la confederació de set sindicats mèdics espanyols de recent creació. L'aturada, que serà d'àmbit estatal, és la resposta del col·lectiu davant l'aprovació del projecte de reforma de l'estatut marc del personal dels serveis de salut per part del Consell de Ministres i l'inici de la tramitació parlamentària.

El text, segons les organitzacions sindicals, perpetua unes condicions laborals "injustes i discriminatòries" per al personal facultatiu.

Els sindicats convocants de la vaga són, a banda d'MC, l'Associació de Metges i Titulats Superiors de Madrid, el Sindicat de Facultatius de Galícia Independents, el Sindicat Mèdic de Galícia, Avanza València, el Sindicat d'Empleats Mèdics de Canàries i el Sindicat Mèdic de Navarra.

Tots ells prioritzaran la unitat d'acció consensuant el calendari d'actuació. L'objectiu compartit és "aconseguir un marc regulatori propi que reconegui la singularitat, la responsabilitat i les especials condicions de formació i exercici de la professió".

En aquesta línia, el Consell Executiu de Metges de Catalunya va acordar aquest dimarts la convocatòria de vaga indefinida a escala catalana coincident "en temps i forma" amb la mobilització estatal.

El secretari general del sindicat, Xavier Lleonart, ha responsabilitzat el Departament de Salut de la persistència de les mobilitzacions dels metges i ha exigit a la consellera que "s'assegui a negociar".

Paral·lelament, i producte de la unió d'esforços de les diferents organitzacions, s'ha presentat la Unió Mèdica i Facultativa (UMYF), una confederació de sindicats que vol ser un instrument de representació amb "autonomia i capacitat legal" per convocar "mobilitzacions a escala estatal".

La confederació està constituïda per sindicats de sis comunitats autònomes que apleguen al voltant de 97.000 facultatius , el 54% de tots els metges de la xarxa pública de salut.

Segons Metges de Catalunya, la UMYF permetrà treballar de manera coordinada per aconseguir que el personal mèdic i facultatiu obtingui un estatut propi que reguli les condicions laborals, professionals i assistencials.

stories.headline: Barcelona reaffirms plan to eliminate 10,000 tourist flats by 2028 after European rules update

sources.body:
Un dia després que la primera tinenta d’alcaldia, Laia Bonet , digués que la futura llei europea d’habitatge assequible avala la decisió del govern de Jaume Collboni d’eliminar els prop de 10.000 pisos turístics que hi ha a la ciutat, l’alcalde ha llegit una declaració institucional en la qual s’ha reafirmat en l’anunci que va fer. “Reforça una decisió que he defensat i que avui torno a remarcar: i és que l’any 2028 desapareixeran les llicències d’habitatges d’ús turístic de la ciutat de Barcelona. Sense marxa enrere”, ha dit Collboni. “Ho vam avançar i ho complirem”, ha afegit.

El text europeu, presentat aquest dimecres a Brussel·les, vol fer front a la crisi de l’habitatge que afecta les principals ciutats europees, a través de la figura de zona tensionada . Aquesta regulació ja existeix a Catalunya i pretén determinar en quines àrees les autoritats podran intervenir el mercat de l’habitatge. Entre els criteris per definir una zona tensionada hi ha que el preu mitjà de l’habitatge sigui igual o superior vuit vegades la renda disponible mitjana dels habitants de la zona.

“Europa reconeix, per primera vegada, que els poders públics tenim el deure d’intervenir quan el mercat, per si sol, no és capaç de garantir un dret tan bàsic com l’accés a l’habitatge”. I, en aquest sentit, “Europa reconeix que les administracions hem de disposar d’instruments per actuar en les zones de mercat tensionat”, i reconeix també “que els habitatges d’ús turístic redueixen la disponibilitat de pisos per als residents i poden alterar el dret de la ciutadania a accedir a un habitatge digne”.

Segons l’alcalde, primer va ser el Tribunal Constitucional qui va avalar la capacitat dels poders públics locals per adoptar mesures en defensa de l’interès general, el dret a quedar-se a la ciutat i la possibilitat de no renovar les llicències d’ús turístic. “I ara és Europa qui avança en el reconeixement de la legitimitat d’aquest tipus d’actuacions”, ha valorat.

El punt de vista de l’alcalde contrasta amb el de la patronal Apartur pel que fa a l’eliminació dels pisos turístics. Per a Apartur, la norma europea fixa “condicions molt estrictes” per justificar “qualsevol restricció” als lloguers de curta durada . I la CEO d’Apartur, Marian Muro considera que la decisió de Collboni d’eliminar els pisos turístics s’ha quedat sense cobertura, “és injustificada, desproporcional i contrària als principis generals del Dret de la Unió Europea” .

Collboni ha destacat tres conceptes de la futura llei europea. D’una banda, la implementació d’àrees tensionades, clau per contenir els preus dels lloguers, a parer seu. Després, el fet que quan un pis deixa de destinar-se a l’ús residencial “pot perjudicar l’oferta residencial i agreujar la crisi de l’habitatge”. I, finalment, la normativa obre també la porta al fet que les autoritats competents “puguin regular altres usos no residencials del sòl o de l’habitatge quan sigui necessari”.
sources.headline: Collboni es reafirma en què eliminarà els pisos turístics i insisteix que Brussel·les ho avala

sources.body:
Unas turistas con maletas tras salir de un piso turístico en el Eixample. / Ferran Nadeu

"No hay marcha atrás. En 2028 desaparecerán los cerca de 10.000 pisos turísticos de Barcelona ", ha reiterado una y otra vez el alcalde Jaume Collboni en una declaración institucional en el ayuntamiento para valorar la futura ley de vivienda asequible presentada oficialmente este miércoles por la Comisión Europea . La propuesta de reglamento supone un marco legal común que define las condiciones en las que las autoridades competentes podrán restringir los alquileres de corta duración. Collboni lo considera un "paso definitivo" que avala las medidas impulsadas hasta ahora tanto por el Gobierno español, como por la Generalitat y el propio consistorio. En especial la promesa municipal de acabar con todas las viviendas de uso turístico de la capital catalana dentro de dos años.

El alcalde considera un "hito histórico sin precedentes " la nueva regulación europea. "Barcelona interpreta que envía un mensaje claro", porque Europa "entiende" que la crisis habitacional "necesita medidas valientes, decididas y proporcionadas", ha enfatizado. Asu juicio, la Comisión "reconoce por primera vez que los poderes públicos locales tienen el deber de intervenir cuando el mercado por sí solo no es capaz de garantizar un derecho tan básico como el acceso a la vivienda", ha señalado. "Queremos garantizar el derecho a quedarse en Barcelona, una ciudad es sostenible solo si quien la hace puede seguir viviendo".

El alcalde Jaume Collboni, durante su comparecencia este miércoles. / Ayuntamiento de Barcelona

El documento presentado es un primer paso, que deberá negociarse de cara a su redacción final. "Hoy empieza una segunda fase" de cara a consolidarlo, ha relatado Collboni, rebatiendo que los " lobbies " nieguen que los pisos con usos turísticos merman la oferta residencial de la ciudad. "Europa lo ha reconocido", ha clamado, subrayando que "los pisos son para vivir, no son un activo financiero". Y "no se trata de una confontación entre actividad económica y vivienda", sino de una cuestión de "modelo de ciudad", ha remachado.

Respondía así a la reacción de la patronal que aglutina a los pisos turísticos de Barcelona, Apartur, y que ayer interpretó que la regulación exigiría "justificar" el resultado una medida como la prohibición de pisos turísticos , algo que creen que el ayuntamiento aún no ha hecho. Pero para el alcalde, Barcelona ya soportó "demasiado tiempo una presión especulativa extraordinaria" que llevó a su gobierno a " actuar", de la mano de otros alcaldes europeos .

"Europa nos da herramientas para aplicar la normativa más ajustada a la realidad", ha afirmado, sobre todo al "reconocer el concepto de zonas tensionadas" que ya se aplica en la capital catalana de la mano de la Ley de Vivienda española, con la limitación de los alquileres, que "ha contenido los precios". Pero el alcalde ve reconocidas y " blindadas " otras iniciativas, como la regulación de usos que en algunos ámbitos, como los pisos turísticos, también lideró Barcelona.
